There is no guard for `obj[k]` being `null`/`undefined`/non-array, so payloads with `*_ids: null` will throw (`Cannot read property 'map' of null`). records.issue_text: Store.js plural *_ids hydration unconditionally deletes key and pushes null/undefined into array when sub-type lookup fails, diverging from singular branch contract
records.rationale: In `store.js` plural hydration (`/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` with `if (m[2])`) does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(...))` and then **always** assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` and `delete obj[k];`. This unconditionally deletes the original `*_ids` key even if lookups fail, and `map` will include `undefined`/`null` elements when `_lookupSubType` can’t resolve an id. By contrast, the singular branch only `delete obj[k]` when `hydrated` is truthy, so the behavior diverges exactly as described.
records.stripped_text: Store.js plural *_ids hydration unconditionally deletes key and pushes null/undefined into array when sub-type lookup fails, diverging from singular branch contract

records.issue_text: Backfilled embeddable host values are not normalized (e.g. https://example.com/1234 copied raw), so the new lower(host) = uri.host lookup fails to match and embeds silently return Discourse::InvalidAccess after migration
records.rationale: The migration backfills `embeddable_hosts` with raw strings via direct SQL, bypassing the model’s `before_validation` normalization (`sub!` stripping scheme/path). In `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, it inserts `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` where `h` can be e.g. `https://example.com/1234`. But `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` later does `host = uri.host` and looks up `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, which will not match a stored value containing scheme/path. This can cause previously-allowed embeds to fail with `Discourse::InvalidAccess` after migration until rows are normalized.

records.issue_text: Migration is irreversible: raw SQL DELETE of embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings is not reversed on rollback, permanently destroying source data with no backup or dual-read window
records.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration uses `def change` but performs non-reversible raw SQL (`execute ... INSERT ...` and `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`). Rails cannot automatically reverse these `execute` calls on rollback, and the final DELETE permanently removes the old `site_settings` source data with no corresponding down/restore logic, making rollback either fail (irreversible) or lose that data.
